key_insight: Neuroevolution, especially evolution strategies, offers a stronger stability-plasticity balance than standard continual RL methods by optimizing directly in weight space.
engineering_relevance: For adaptive control and sequential decision systems, this suggests a practical route to continual learning that can retain prior capabilities while adapting to new operating conditions.
method: Compare evolution strategies and genetic algorithms against continual RL and population-based RL across multiple changing environments.
Analyze return landscapes around learned policies to measure how wide and overlapping task-solution neighborhoods are in weight space.
Test whether novelty search increases plasticity and examine how perturbation robustness relates to forgetting.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates a wide range of environments and task changes, from a few hundred to million-parameter policies, and links overlap of solution neighborhoods to stability-plasticity performance.
watch_item: The strongest plasticity gains can come with increased forgetting, so deployment should consider how much prior-task retention is acceptable.
